dedupe_keys.name: gleamviz global epidemic and mobility model simulator for scenario analysis of infectious disease spread

description: GLEAMviz is a simulator for realistic scenarios of the global spread of infectious diseases, built on the Global Epidemic and Mobility (GLEAM) model. The GLEAMviz project developed it for researchers and students in epidemiology and to support policy making and emergency planning for highly pathogenic diseases. The system has a server component whose engine runs GLEAM, a metapopulation model combining population data with air travel and commuting mobility (Van den Broeck et al. 2011), and a desktop client in which users define arbitrary compartmental disease models, set up simulations through a visual interface and explore results with maps, charts and other widgets. Coverage is global, with outputs by subpopulation and country. The client is freely available to download from the project website, and simulations are executed on the project's server. Caveats: the simulation engine is not open source, results depend on the disease parameters users choose, and the model predicts infections, not health system load, so hospital demand must be derived separately. Simulation uses: generating epidemic curves and importation timing for healthcare surge planning, testing travel restrictions, and providing infection scenarios that drive hospital capacity models. Related records: OpenABM-Covid19 (model-openabm-covid19) is an open agent-based epidemic model and CDC FluSurge (model-cdc-flusurge) turns pandemic scenarios into hospital demand.
